hints: Calculate the gravitational potential energy lost as the block descends $1.6\text{ m}$: $\Delta E_p = mgh = 15(10)(1.6) = 240\text{ J}$.
Calculate the kinetic energy at the top ($\frac{1}{2}(15)(2^2) = 30\text{ J}$) and at the bottom ($\frac{1}{2}(15)(4^2) = 120\text{ J}$).
Form the work-energy balance: $\Delta E_p + E_{k,\text{top}} - W_{\text{resistance}} = E_{k,\text{bottom}}$, and solve for $W_{\text{resistance}} = 150\text{ J}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the potential energy lost and the kinetic energy at the top and bottom of the plane:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 15(10)(1.6) = 240\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k,\text{top}} = \frac{1}{2}(15)(2^2) = 30\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k,\text{bottom}} = \frac{1}{2}(15)(4^2) = 120\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle:
$$\Delta E_p + E_{k,\text{top}} - W_R = E_{k,\text{bottom}}$$
$$240 + 30 - W_R = 120$$
$$270 - W_R = 120 \implies W_R = 270 - 120 = 150\text{ J}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work–Energy Principle: Finds PE loss = 240 J, KE top = 30 J, KE bottom = 120 J, and determines work done against resistance = 150 J.

teacher_walkthrough:
Name the work-energy principle: the total initial mechanical energy (potential plus kinetic) minus the work done against resistive forces equals the final mechanical energy:
$$E_{p,\text{initial}} + E_{k,\text{initial}} - W_{\text{resistance}} = E_{k,\text{final}}$$

Calculate the decrease in gravitational potential energy as the $15\text{ kg}$ block descends a vertical height of $1.6\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = (15)(10)(1.6) = 240\text{ J}$$

Calculate the kinetic energy at the top where $u = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{top}} = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(15)(2^2) = \frac{1}{2}(15)(4) = 30\text{ J}$$

Calculate the kinetic energy at the bottom where $v = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{bottom}} = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(15)(4^2) = \frac{1}{2}(15)(16) = 120\text{ J}$$

Substitute the calculated values into the work-energy equation:
$$240 + 30 - W = 120$$
$$270 - W = 120$$

Subtract 120 from 270 to find the work done against resistance:
$$W = 270 - 120 = 150\text{ J}$$
